title: The compute-efficient frontier
goal:
Section 6 turns the fitted laws into a recipe for a fixed compute budget $C_\text{min}$ measured in PF-days. The starter holds the constants from Equation 1.3, Equation 1.4, and Appendix A. Write:

- `optimal_loss(c)`, $L(C_\text{min}) = (C_c^\text{min} / C_\text{min})^{\alpha_C^\text{min}}$ (Equation 1.3).
- `compute_for_loss(loss)`, the inverse: the compute that reaches a target loss.
- `optimal_model_size(c)`, $N_\text{opt} = N_e\, C_\text{min}^{0.73}$ (Equation 6.1 and Table 6).
- `optimal_tokens(c)`, $D_\text{opt} = D_e\, C_\text{min}^{0.27}$ for one epoch (Table 6).
- `critical_batch_size(loss)`, $B_\text{crit}(L) = B_* / L^{1/\alpha_B}$ (Equation 1.4).

The tests also check that the allocation is consistent with $C = 6NBS$: the exponents $0.73$ and $0.27$ sum to 1, so $6 N D / C_\text{min}$ is the same at every budget.
hints: `compute_for_loss` solves $L = (C_c / C)^{\alpha}$ for $C$: raise both sides to the power $-1/\alpha$, then multiply by $C_c$.
Every function except `compute_for_loss` is one line. The check that matters is whether it round-trips: `compute_for_loss(optimal_loss(c))` must return `c`.
`critical_batch_size` takes the loss, not the compute. A lower loss needs a larger batch, so the exponent on `loss` in the denominator is positive.
